title: We are all hypocrites
hookLine: people often say the church is a hospital for sinners, not a museum of saints

cards: "They're all hypocrites." It gets said about churches at family dinners, in comment sections, sometimes with anger and sometimes with a tired shrug. And there's a reply some Christians give that surprises people: yes.
All of us. A saying gets passed around about it: the church is a hospital for sinners, not a museum of saints. Nobody seems sure who said it first, and it isn't a Bible verse.
But it points at something the Bible says plainly, and says first about its own people.

teach.h: SEEN OF MEN: GOODNESS AS A SHOW.
teach.b: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus speaks to the crowd and to his own disciples about how they give and pray. Don't sound a trumpet when you give to the poor, he says.
Don't pray on the street corners like the hypocrites, "that they may be seen of men." A hypocrite, in his picture, is someone performing goodness for an audience.
Then comes an image that's almost a cartoon: "Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother's eye."

teach.h: THE BEAM IN YOUR OWN EYE.
teach.b: A wooden beam sticking out of your face while you squint at the speck in someone else's. Some readers hear a joke in it, and then a wince. Paul doesn't claim to have it together.

teach.h: THE GOOD THAT I WOULD I DO NOT.
teach.b: In Romans he writes: "For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do." The gap between what he believes and what he does is a place he lives.
And he widens the circle to include everyone: "For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God." All. That's where all of us comes from.

And Jesus said who he came for: "I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance." So when someone says the church is full of hypocrites, a Christian who has read these texts can agree without flinching.
In its own scriptures, the church was never meant to be a gallery of finished people. The danger Jesus names isn't the struggle. It's the performance: pretending the beam isn't there.

how: Church services in several traditions include a general confession said together by the whole congregation, in which everyone, clergy included, admits their sin before God; Catholic and Orthodox Christians also confess privately to a priest.

games.q: what does “we are all hypocrites” mean?
o: an excuse that lets anyone do as they please
an honest admission that everyone falls short
a claim that churchgoers are worse than others

games.q: the hypocrite and the beam — tap the pairs.

s: in the Sermon on the Mount, the hypocrites perform goodness to be seen
they pray on the street corners, that they may be seen of men.
Paul writes that he always does the good he wants to
for the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do.
'a hospital for sinners, not a museum of saints' is a Bible verse
it's a saying people pass around. the verse it echoes: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

games.q: you can clearly see a speck in your friend's eye, a small fault of theirs. according to Jesus, what comes first?
o: point it out right away, kindly.
cast the beam out of your own eye.
games.why: first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; then you'll see clearly to help with the speck. the speck still matters. the order is the point.

practice: Start with someone else's speck, a fault in another person that gets under your skin, then turn the question around: where does some version of that live in you, or what value do you talk about but don't live?
Don't punish yourself; look at the beam plainly, the way you'd look at a splinter you finally want out. Name it honestly to yourself, and if you pray, name it to God.

wordCard.voice: We are all hypocrites. Not an excuse but an admission: Paul's all have sinned, said with the word we.

orig.note: Greek: hypocrite — the word behind "Thou hypocrite" in Matthew 7:5.

carryVoice: Your line: all of us. A hospital for sinners, not a museum of saints. Until tomorrow.
